pages.notes: Lecture50 Developing An Emotion Engine For Robots cover, footer1.
Agenda including state machines, human model, affective computing, FER/SER/multimodal emotion and challenges.
Same words may have different tone/context/expressed affect. Illustration not a measurement of actual feelings; goal empathetic interaction.
Diagram STT→intent parsing→LLM, then TTS to user and separate ROS state-machine→robot-action branch. Text-only baseline ignores nonverbal cues, not every possible system.
Text-based estimated human affect updates simulated robot response state. Separate human and robot models. Explicit simulation rather than consciousness.
States, transitions, triggers and output actions are distinct. User interaction, context and internal variables can trigger changes.

Actual polar figure places welcoming/happy/friend/curious on left and frustrated/stranger/sad/distant on right. Yellow circles individual values; purple resultant line; arcs extrema. Angles differ from notebook table. Title missing E in Emotion is cosmetic.

Printed r=(rmax−rmin)/2 and theta=(thetamax−thetamin)/2 are half spans, not arithmetic midpoints. On stated0..100 bounds radius≤50, conflicting with >55 branch. Neutral45..55 described as center but polar radius0 is geometric origin. Under55 outside45..55 unresolved by printed rule. Circular wrapping requires separate handling.

OppositeMagnitude=100−ActiveValue;75/25 example. Chosen complementary software constraint, not universal human psychology. Scan radial extrema and associatedangles, distinct from notebook centered-vector sum.

Human figure happyup/saddown, friendlyleft/distantright; upper-left happyfriendly. Initial middle is an estimate, not measured neutral affect. Figure boxes say Robot last/next state despite human-model caption, preserve label mismatch.

Pseudocode loadengine/LLM/memory then input→estimate→humanupdate→robotupdate→response(input,emotion,robotstate,memory)→save→display→visualize. Link points official notebook; exact implementation differs from printed polar half-span equations.
Affect encompasses feelings/emotions/moods. Multiple observable facial/voice/body cues supplement text; inference not direct internal-state measurement.
Recognition analyzes expression patterns; expression generation synthesizes them. Accurate-human-observer performance is a goal, not a measured achievement or direct access to feelings.

Pretrained model transfer, three adaptation strategies, processed CK+ training, saved model, testing and comparison loop. Reusing a test set for strategy selection would contaminate evaluation; keep validation selection separate.

VGG16 five convolutional blocks (64,128,256,512,512), max-pool2×2, classifier Flatten/GlobalAveragePool→Dense256→Dropout0.2→Dense128→Dropout0.2→Dense8→softmax. Full-fine-tune text means entire network despite bracket layout. Small data can overfit.

FER2013 grayscale, RAF-DB grayscale/RGB, AffectNet grayscale/RGB. AffectNet supports categorical and continuous valence/arousal targets. Shown photos are dataset examples, not independent judgments of the people.

Seven displayed classifier labels neutral, anger, sadness, surprise, happiness, disgust, fear. Source Ekman attribution needs qualification: neutral is not his seventh universal-emotion label. No individual emotional state inferred.

Valence/arousal numeric ranges -1..1 and supplied V0.63,A0.77. Source energy-of-image wording is misleading; valence is negativity/positivity, arousal activation. The provided positive/high values are read as annotations, not new face inference.

Outer axis names conflict with numeric sample placement: annotations support x=valence,y=arousal; negative V left, positive A above. Use stated coordinate convention, retaining the printed-label conflict.

SER waveform→pitch,rate,energy,MFCC features→deep model→estimated label. Illustrated 90/5/3/2 scores total100 but do not establish calibration or actual private emotion. Tiny MFCC inset omits detail and is not a complete derivation.
Face, voice and language features combine; remaining modalities can help only if the model supports missing inputs, not a guaranteed robustness claim.
Emotion engine integrates face/voice/language estimates to influence behavior and dialogue, not direct measurement of internal feelings.
User input→emotion estimate→conversation memory→dialogue planning→robot response. Memory emphasized in this architecture, not exclusive to social robots.
Speech style, facial display, LEDs, arms and head motions are output modalities; coordinated context-sensitive cues matter.
Healthcare, education, customer service, home/elderly assistance applications. Individual variation, mixed emotion, occlusion/lighting, culture, privacy and ethics are explicitly listed.
Summary restates cue-based inference, multimodal fusion, memory/planning and applications; no new equation or algorithm branch.
References: Govers2024; Li/Deng/Du2017 RAF-DB; Wang2006 3D expressions; Ekman/Friesen1971. Bibliographic rather than new examinable content.
References: AffectNet Mollahosseini/Hasani/Mahoor2017 and Saini/Pathak2024 chapter. No new algorithm.
Thank-you slide only.

notebookNotes: Inspected source cells5,7,9,11,13,15,17,19,21; no installation, service or live model/UI. Human inference and robot simulation distinguished. Raw multi-axis resultant may exceed100; only plotted radius clips. Confidence threshold is strict <0.30. Unassigned robot axes persist across turns. Classifier encodes six history dictionaries within one prompt, reply includes eight as role messages. add_turn retains twelve message dictionaries, not twelve user/assistant pairs. All numerical checks use synthetic inputs.
